No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result MIT Solve, NASENI And PICTT On Strong Footing To Enhance Delta-2, DELT-Her Innovations by Innocent Odoh 7 seconds ago in News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in Boston, United States (US) under its innovative programme MIT Solve launched 10 years to fund global solutions, is set to partner with the Presidential Implementation Committee on Technology Transfer (PICTT) and National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI).
This partnership is aimed at scaling up Nigerian innovators with the technical skills and funding required to make them provide world class solutions that will establish Nigeria within the global map digital solutions.
Under this programme ten Nigerian innovators from DELTA-2 Programme and Developing Engineering Leaders Through Her (DELT-Her) cohorts are set for a six- month acceleration programme at MIT Solve, Boston Massachusetts to create pathways for promising homegrown solutions to scale and achieve greater impact.
This programme, which was organized by PICTT and NASENI, was carefully framed to strengthen the Nigerian innovators with technical skills and mentorship that would help their innovations move to the commercial stage and secure a valuable place for Nigerian products into the international market.
MIT Solve is an open-innovation initiative from MIT that provides social impact and entrepreneurship services, connecting startups with funding and resources to address global challenges.
Chairman of PICTT, Dr. Dahiru Mohammed, speaking in a media briefing at PICTT office in Abuja on Thursday said 10 out of 20 innovators from the DELTA 2 and DELT-Her cohorts whose solutions are at various stages of scale readiness, after pitching to a team of judges, will be selected to partake in the six-month acceleration programme with MIT Solve, Boston Massachusetts.
He said drawing on an intake assessment of individual and cohort needs, MIT Solve will design targeted programming to help innovators refine their business models, strengthen their pitches, and build the entrepreneurial leadership needed to grow.
According to a statement from NASENI, throughout the six months programme, cohort convenings will bring innovators together with peers and invited ecosystem stakeholders, including industry associations, academic institutions, and other local partners, to build the ecosystem and visibility that early-stage Nigerian innovators need to scale.
According to Dr. Mohammed, the uniqueness of this initiative is that it has government support and backing and provides the Delta-2 and DELT-Her innovators access to global partners to support them to scale and become commercially viable.
He said “the Delta-2 Programme is focused on helping entrepreneurs access funding and partners from across the world to build on their innovations or to undertake research development and innovation activities that would bring about commercially viable products that would help Nigeria’s industrial development.
“The Second initiative is DELT-Her which focuses on female engineers across Nigeria to access opportunities to showcase their research and innovations and get them to the market”, he added, noting that Nigeria has below average numbers of female engineers compared to the global average.
He said the partnership between NASENI, PICTT and MIT Solve is a “game changer” that will fast track the scaling up of innovators from DELTA-2 and DELT-Her programmes, even as he lauded President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for providing the level playing ground and founding for NASENI and PICTT to support Nigerian Innovators.
Some of the beneficiaries who spoke to the media included Prof. Christopher Ihueze( Delta-2), Tseko Torkwase Priscilla (DELT-Her)Riskat Adeby (DELT-Her) and Dr. Ilorter Grace(Delta-2) and they have their innovations in different areas to provide solutions.
Among the judges that will select the 10 finalists for the MIT Solve accelerator programme include Halima Tauheed, MIT Solve; Olamide Apejoye, Project Coordinator; Musa Ali Baba, Consultant to PICTT, Chief Tunde Rahman, judge and others.
The Delta-2 program currently funds researchers on various R&D projects across the country. The Delta-2 Programme is a bilateral applied research, development, and innovation initiative by the NASENI in partnership with the Technology Agency of the Czech Republic (TA CR) via the PICTT.
Developing Engineering Leaders Through Her (DELT-Her 2.0) is an initiative that seeks to create opportunities for women in engineering, by attracting and supporting innovative engineering ideas which would ultimately be mentored and developed into startup companies.
The investment is aimed at fostering a more inclusive and diverse engineering practice landscape in Nigeria as well as to build a collaborative network of stakeholders including tertiary institutions, business, and industry leaders, who would enable a more supportive environment for women in engineering.
It is also aimed to inspire the next generation of female engineers in Nigeria by making female engineering success stories more visible to them. The success stories from the first phase of this initiative would be projected to boost school-age girls across the country, with the aim of creating a paradigm shift to favor their choice of engineering as a lifelong career.
DELT-Her is inspired by global projects from the Anita Borg Institute, Girl Up! at the UN Foundation, Applied Science Technologists and Technicians of British Columbia among others.
In 2025, NASENI in partnership with PICTT granted the sum of N229 million to 14 women awardees of the DELT-Her, which the Executive Vice Chairman/Chief Executive of NASENI, Mr. Khalil Suleiman Halilu had described as an opportunity platform through which women can turn bold engineering ideas into solutions that change the world.
The 14 women engineers emerged as awardees, receiving N229 million in grant funding to advance their innovative projects across critical sectors such as agriculture, clean energy, health, mobility, digital security and environmental sustainability.
According to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), women make up an average of 22% of the total number of engineering and technology graduates. The largest disparity is found in postgraduate enrolment between male and female in engineering and technology and this was estimated at 12.06% for female while male enrolment was 87.4%.
Therefore it was apt that NASENI’s has expanded investment in this sector and the agency has channeled critical resources aimed at creating a shift in this paradigm.
